evidence.section: 4.1 Superplastic behaviour and effective activation energy
evidence.quote: Grain boundary sliding (GBS) is the predominant deformation mechanism during superplastic flow for most fine-grained materials with strain rate expone nts of approximately 0.5 and an activation energy which is either equal to the activation energy for lattice diffusion (Q L) or to the activation energy for grain-boundary diffusion (Q GB ) [1,49].

evidence.quote: TEM analysis of the microstructure confirmed that the coarse 1.5 µm Al 3Ni particles provide nucleation sites for new grains and a larger number of nuclei for recrystallization due to the PSN.

evidence.section: 4.2 Evolution of grain structure and analysis of the dislocation structure
evidence.quote: Increased dynamics in the recrystallised volume dur ing superplastic deformation indicates that dynamic recrystallization occurs very quickly in all oy B possibly due to particle stimulated nucleation (PSN) and dynamic recrystallization is slow in alloy A due to a low volume fraction of coarse particles.
